anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : The application issues inefficient or over-broad SQL or transaction patterns that force the engine to scan, sort, or lock far more data than business logic actually requires.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standby or subscriber nodes fall behind because they cannot receive, write, or apply the primary’s log stream at the rate it is generated.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer is saturated in throughput, IOPS, or latency, throttling reads, writes, and durability flushes across data, temp, and log files.

When all three anomalies arise together, the database exhibits extreme and persistent slowness across both primary and replica tiers: primary sessions show long-tail statement latencies, high read and write waits, and prolonged transaction lifetimes; slow-query and statement-statistics views list the same heavyweight SQL repeatedly. On replicas, log-position gaps widen rapidly, apply lag grows from seconds to minutes or hours, relay logs bloat, and read-only workloads return increasingly stale data. Administrators observe escalating disk-queue depths, soaring device-level latency, checkpoints that take longer to complete, and log segments accumulating because replication cannot advance. Failover readiness deteriorates, and application retries may amplify concurrency and locking conflicts, masking whether the bottleneck is in SQL design, storage, or replication.

Causally, inefficient SQL and long-running transactions generated by the SQL Workload Logic Anomaly create large volumes of table and index I/O as well as oversized redo bursts. These heavy I/O demands collide with pre-existing or induced Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly, causing data-file reads, temp spills, and log flushes to queue behind saturated devices. The inflated redo stream must traverse the replication channel; however, the same storage bottlenecks now slow both transmission and apply on replicas, triggering the Replication Synchronization Anomaly. As replicas lag, the primary is prevented from recycling log segments, further increasing write pressure on the already stressed storage layer. The feedback loop among verbose workload, throttled storage, and backlog in replication amplifies each symptom, making the overall system progressively less responsive and complicating root-cause isolation.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
